title: Conjecture 14
statement_text: There exist functions $g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for any $c \geq 1$, every graph $G$ with growth $f_G(r) \leq cr$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of $T \boxtimes K_{g(c)}$ for some tree $T$ with growth $f_T(r) \leq h(c)r$.
context_text: The growth of a (possibly infinite) graph $G$ is the function $f_G:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$ where $f_G(r)$ is the supremum of $|V(H)|$ over all subgraphs $H$ of $G$ of radius at most $r$; a class has linear growth if this is $O(r)$. The strong product $A\boxtimes B$ has vertex set $V(A)\times V(B)$, with $(v,w)$ and $(v',w')$ adjacent if ($vv'\in E(A)$ and $w=w'$) or ($v=v'$ and $ww'\in E(B)$) or ($vv'\in E(A)$ and $ww'\in E(B)$). Thus $T\boxtimes K_t$ is the blow-up of $T$ obtained by replacing each vertex by a $K_t$ and each edge by a $K_{t,t}$. The authors' main result is that every graph with $f_G(r)\le cr$ has treewidth at most $49c^2+30c$. Such a graph also has maximum degree at most $c-1$, so known results give that it is a subgraph of $T\boxtimes K_{\lfloor 882c^3\rfloor}$ for some tree $T$. But $T$ may have exponential growth (e.g. a complete binary tree), and then so does the product. The conjecture asks for a tree of linear growth instead. This would roughly characterise graphs of linear growth, since every subgraph $H$ of $T\boxtimes K_{g(c)}$ then has $f_H(r)\le g(c)h(c)r$. The authors make the analogous conjecture for polynomial growth $f_G(r)\le cr^d$, with a product of $d$ trees of linear growth and a clique $K_{g(c,d)}$.
paper_title: Graphs of Linear Growth have Bounded Treewidth

title: Conjecture 15
statement_text: There exist functions $g : \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $h : \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for any $c > 1$ and $d \in \mathbb{N}$, every graph $G$ with growth $f_G(r) \leq cr^d$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of $T_1 \boxtimes \cdots \boxtimes T_d \boxtimes K_{g(c,d)}$, where each $T_i$ is a tree of growth $f_{T_i}(r) \leq h(c,d)r$.
context_text: Conjecture 15 generalises Conjecture 14 to graphs of degree-$d$ polynomial growth. If true, it would approximately characterise such graphs, since any subgraph $H$ of $T_1 \boxtimes \cdots \boxtimes T_d \boxtimes K_{g(c,d)}$ satisfies $f_H(r) \leq g(c,d)(h(c,d)r)^d \in O(r^d)$. This is motivated by a result of Krauthgamer and Lee showing that every graph of growth $f_G(r) \leq r^d$ embeds as a subgraph of the strong product of $O(d \log d)$ sufficiently long paths.
paper_title: Graphs of Linear Growth have Bounded Treewidth
